title: Classes, Value Objects, and Encapsulation
summary: Model valid state with constructors, private properties, readonly values, methods, interfaces, namespaces, and dependency boundaries.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Classes, Value Objects, and Encapsulation
Verify contracts with lint, runtime, and test evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: A class combines state and behavior. Keep properties private when arbitrary assignment could violate invariants, and validate constructor input before the object becomes observable. Readonly properties can be initialized once and support value objects, but nested referenced objects may still be mutable. Interfaces describe behavior required by consumers; avoid large interfaces that force unrelated methods. Namespaces prevent collisions and map naturally to Composer PSR-4 autoloading. Inject collaborators rather than constructing infrastructure inside domain methods.
keyPoints: A class combines state and behavior.
commonMistakes: returning from finally can obscure earlier results or errors
public mutable fields permit invalid state

sections.heading: Worked PHP example
sections.content:
Predict types, failures, and output, then lint, run, and compare the evidence.

In practical software engineering with PHP, understanding runtime behavior, boundary cases, and diagnostic evidence is essential for reliable deployment.

codeExamples.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
final class Progress {
  public function __construct(private int $percent) { if ($percent < 0 || $percent > 100) throw new InvalidArgumentException('percent'); }
  public function percent(): int { return $this->percent; }
}
echo (new Progress(75))->percent() . "\n";
